schema_notes: Catalog of curated animation packs and individual animations from free/CC0 sources. The Animations view renders cards from this file. Each entry's 'prompt' field is pre-filled into chat on click, the AI then guides the user through the download + import flow (Quixel Bridge, Epic Launcher marketplace, direct ZIP fetch, etc.).

assets.name: UE Animation Starter Pack
assets.description: Epic's classic locomotion pack. 10 animations on the Mannequin skeleton, perfect starter for a ThirdPerson character.
assets.prompt:
Guide me through installing Epic's 'Animation Starter Pack' into my project.

Steps:
1. Open Epic Games Launcher → Unreal Engine → Marketplace.
2. Search for 'Animation Starter Pack' by Epic Games.
3. Click 'Free', then 'Add to Project' and select this project (UE 5.5).
4. After it lands, the animations appear at /Game/AnimStarterPack/.
5. Retarget them to my current character (BP_ThirdPersonCharacter uses the UE5 Mannequin skeleton) via the Retarget Manager if needed.
6. Report which animations are now available and which BP would use them.

assets.name: Mixamo Idle Loop
assets.description: Single looping idle animation. Quick to grab, retarget in seconds with Mixamo's naming convention.
assets.prompt:
Walk me through grabbing a free Idle Loop from Mixamo and retargeting it to my UE5 Mannequin character.

Steps:
1. Open https://www.mixamo.com/, log in with an Adobe account.
2. Upload the UE5 Mannequin FBX (or use Mixamo's Y-Bot as a proxy) as the skeleton.
3. Search 'Idle', pick a looping idle, click Download.
4. In the download dialog: Format=FBX for Unreal, Skin=With Skin, Frames per Second=30, Keyframe Reduction=None.
5. Import the .fbx into UE at /Game/LocoAI/Animations/Mixamo/Idle_Loop.
6. Create an IK Retargeter if the source skeleton differs from mine.
7. Retarget the animation to my current BP's skeleton and report the result path.

assets.name: Kenney, Animated Character Pack
assets.description: Low-poly animated characters with basic combat + locomotion. Stylized, no attribution required.
assets.prompt:
Help me download the 'Kenney Animated Characters' pack from kenney.nl and import one character into my project.

Steps:
1. Open https://kenney.nl/assets/animated-characters-2 in my browser.
2. Download the ZIP (CC0, no attribution required).
3. Extract to a temp folder.
4. The pack has FBX files per character. Pick one character (e.g., 'adventurer') and import its FBX into /Game/LocoAI/Characters/Adventurer using Python + AssetToolsHelpers.
5. The pack includes skeletal mesh + animations (idle, walk, run, jump, attack, die). Import each .fbx in the subfolder.
6. Report the full list of imported assets.

assets.name: Mixamo Combat Pack
assets.description: Collection of ~8 combat animations. Download as a single pack via Mixamo's 'Character Pack' option.
assets.prompt:
Guide me through downloading a Mixamo combat pack and importing it.

Steps:
1. Go to https://www.mixamo.com/ and sign in.
2. Select a character (or use Y-Bot).
3. Search 'Sword Swing', pick 2-3 variants.
4. Search 'Block', 'Hit Reaction', 'Death', add each to the My Animations queue.
5. Use 'Pack' download to bundle them into one ZIP (FBX, 30fps, With Skin).
6. Extract. Import each .fbx as a skeletal animation at /Game/LocoAI/Animations/Combat/.
7. Retarget to my active BP's skeleton.

assets.name: UE Free MoCap Sample
assets.description: Epic's free MoCap sample featuring unarmed combat moves. Clean motion capture quality.
assets.prompt:
Install Epic's 'MoCap' free sample pack into my UE5 project.

Steps:
1. Epic Games Launcher → Unreal Engine → Marketplace → search 'MoCap sample' by Epic.
2. Click Free and Add to Project.
3. After install, animations land at /Game/MoCap/.
4. List which animations are available and help me wire one into BP_ThirdPersonCharacter's AnimBlueprint.

assets.name: Mixamo Emote Set
assets.description: Fun emote animations, wave, clap, dance, salute, cheer. Great for multiplayer taunts or NPC life.
assets.prompt:
Help me grab a set of emote animations (wave, clap, dance, salute, cheer) from Mixamo and import them.

Steps:
1. https://www.mixamo.com/ → sign in.
2. Search each emote: 'Waving', 'Clapping', 'Dancing Twerk' (or another dance), 'Salute', 'Cheering'.
3. Add to My Animations.
4. Pack download → FBX for Unreal.
5. Import each .fbx at /Game/LocoAI/Animations/Emotes/.
6. Retarget to my character.

assets.name: Quadruped Starter Pack
assets.description: Wolf skeletal mesh + locomotion cycles. Good base for any 4-legged enemy or companion.
assets.prompt:
Install Epic's 'Quadruped Starter Pack' (or equivalent free wolf/dog pack) from the Marketplace.

Steps:
1. Open Epic Games Launcher → Marketplace → search 'quadruped' filtered by Free.
2. Pick a free quadruped pack.
3. Add to this project.
4. After install, list the animations and skeletal mesh paths.
5. Create a BP_WolfNPC actor wrapping the skeletal mesh + a basic AnimBlueprint with an Idle→Walk blend.

legal_notes: Only assets with commercial-use-allowed licenses are listed (CC0, Mixamo free tier, UE Marketplace free assets).
Some sources require an account (Epic Games, Adobe), that is a one-time step per developer.
License text per asset is the responsibility of the downloader to preserve and attribute where required (Kenney = CC0, no attribution; Mixamo = free with Adobe ToS; UE assets = UE EULA).
